tool.name: Lefse
tool.command:
@SHELL_OPTIONS@
## create symlinks to input datasets ln -s '$otu' shared.dat && ln -s '$design' design.dat &&
## collect the arguments of the mothur command in a list and join them with ## commas, so that the command can never end with a trailing comma #set $mothur_args = [] #silent $mothur_args.append("shared=shared.dat") #silent $mothur_args.append("design=design.dat") #if $class: #silent $mothur_args.append("class=" + str($class)) #end if #if $sclass: #silent $mothur_args.append("subclass=" + str($sclass)) #end if #if $label: #silent $mothur_args.append("label=" + str(str($label).replace(",","-"))) #end if #if $sets: #silent $mothur_args.append("sets=" + str(str($sets).replace(",","-"))) #end if #silent $mothur_args.append("aalpha=" + str($aalpha)) #silent $mothur_args.append("walpha=" + str($walpha)) #silent $mothur_args.append("lda=" + str($lda)) #silent $mothur_args.append("iters=" + str($iters)) #silent $mothur_args.append("fboots=" + str($fboots)) #silent $mothur_args.append("strict=" + str($strict)) #silent $mothur_args.append("minc=" + str($minc)) #silent $mothur_args.append("wilc=" + str($wilc)) #silent $mothur_args.append("curv=" + str($curv)) #silent $mothur_args.append("norm=" + str($norm))
echo 'lefse(${",".join($mothur_args)})' | mothur | tee mothur.out.log

param.label: design - assigns groups to sets
param.help: design has 2 TAB-separated columns with a 'group' header: group (col 1) and grouping (col 2), see the mothur design file documentation

param.label: sets - Which of the sets in your design file you would like to analyze?
param.help: separate sets by dashes or commas, e.g. set1,set2 or set1-set2-set3

param.label: class -indicate the which category you would like used for the Kruskal Wallis analysis
param.help: If none is provided first category is used

param.label: subclass - indicate the which category you would like used for the Kruskal Wallis analysis
param.help: If none is provided second category is used

param.label: aalpha - alpha value for the Krukal Wallis Anova test
walpha - alpha value for the Wilcoxon test
lda - threshold on the absolute value of the logarithmic LDA score
iters - number of bootstrap iteration for LDA
fboots - set the subsampling fraction value for each bootstrap iteration
strict - set the multiple testing correction options
param.help: 0 no correction (more strict, default), 1 correction for independent comparisons, 2 correction for independent comparison

param.label: minc - minimum number of samples per subclass for performing wilcoxon test
wilc - indicate whether to perform the Wilcoxon test
curv - whether perform the wilcoxon testing the Curtis's approach (beta)
norm - multiply relative abundances by 1000000
param.help: Recommended when very low values are present
